dedupe_keys.name: boston building emissions reduction and disclosure ordinance berdo reported data

description: Annual reported energy and water use of large Boston buildings under the Building Emissions Reduction and Disclosure Ordinance, published by the City of Boston Environment Department on Analyze Boston. BERDO, amended in 2021, sets emissions standards that fall over time toward net zero by 2050 for residential buildings with 15 or more units and non-residential buildings of 20,000 square feet or more, and requires owners to report energy and water use each year by May 15. The dataset offers one file per reporting year, mostly as Excel workbooks, with data dictionaries, and links to interactive compliance maps. Contents: property details such as address, size and units, electricity, gas and heating oil use, water use, emissions and compliance status. Coverage: the city of Boston, from 2015 data reported in 2016 onward. Data for 2021 and earlier were reported under the older Building Energy Reporting and Disclosure Ordinance, which covered buildings of 35,000 square feet or 25 units and more and had no emissions requirement, so years are not directly comparable. Access: open download. Licence: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License; cost free. The record was last modified on 3 March 2026 in the CKAN record. Useful for city-scale building energy and retrofit planning models and for assessing the effect of emissions standards.
